speaker: Lena
text: Review of the package registry mirror for build farms. Workers wait on public registries.

speaker: Omar
text: 900 workers at peak, 70 percent Linux and rest macOS. Egress is capped at 2 gigabits per region.

speaker: Priya
text: Package should be available in a region within two minutes of first request anywhere.

speaker: Lena
text: Preserve upstream signatures and checksums, no repacking.

speaker: Omar
text: Start with a pull-through cache in front of public registries.

speaker: Priya
text: Yes, pull-through on first miss, then serve from regional mirror.

speaker: Lena
text: npm and PyPI first; Maven can wait.

speaker: Omar
text: Java builds have same pain. Include Maven Central day one.

speaker: Lena
text: Fine, npm, PyPI, Maven. No Docker images; those use container registry.

speaker: Priya
text: S3-compatible object store with metadata in Postgres?

speaker: Omar
text: Metadata in Postgres makes eviction easy. Objects immutable, keyed by registry and digest.

speaker: Lena
text: Accepted: object store plus Postgres metadata.

speaker: Priya
text: Shared cache, auth per build identity; namespace is audit only.

speaker: Omar
text: Retention, I put 30 days after last access in draft.

speaker: Lena
text: Make that 60 days, disk is cheap.

speaker: Priya
text: Sixty works.

speaker: Omar
text: Was that sixty days or sixty gigabytes?

speaker: Lena
text: Days. And when I say cut it in half, that means thirty from sixty, not original thirty.

speaker: Priya
text: Hard cap maybe 4 terabytes per region.

speaker: Omar
text: At 900 workers that could evict hot packages. Could be 8 terabytes.

speaker: Lena
text: Use 8 TB per region, alert at 80 percent, accepted for first rollout.

speaker: Priya
text: Replication between regions?

speaker: Omar
text: I would not replicate proactively. First request in a region fetches upstream.

speaker: Lena
text: We need popular packages copied to all regions within two minutes of first request anywhere.

speaker: Priya
text: Regional Kafka topic announces digest availability.

speaker: Omar
text: Could have cache daemons poll each other.

speaker: Lena
text: No, choose regional Kafka notification; regions fetch immutable object.

speaker: Priya
text: Agreed.

speaker: Omar
text: Upstream TLS, signed metadata, builders should not have write access.

speaker: Priya
text: Service account only writer; build workers get region-scoped read-only credentials.

speaker: Lena
text: Require provenance attestation?

speaker: Omar
text: Upstream signature and checksum required. Attestation format can follow, not launch gate.

speaker: Priya
text: Open whether to store and expose provenance attestations. Omar, check what build platform emits?

speaker: Omar
text: I can inventory that by Thursday.

speaker: Lena
text: Platform leads want more time for quarterly rebuilds, retention 90 days.

speaker: Priya
text: Then storage cap needs reconsideration, 8 TB might be tight.

speaker: Omar
text: Let us double that, from 8 TB to 16 TB per region, for headroom.

speaker: Lena
text: Agreed, 16 TB and 90 days since last access.

speaker: Priya
text: Cold packages cheap but metadata scans get expensive.

speaker: Omar
text: Expire metadata and blobs together. No separate archive tier v1.

speaker: Lena
text: Fine, expiration coordinated.

speaker: Priya
text: Regional control plane?

speaker: Omar
text: Cache service serves admin API, no extra control plane.

speaker: Lena
text: Agreed, one service per region, admin endpoint co-located.

speaker: Priya
text: Rollout canary is 10 teams, then 50, then all build teams.

speaker: Lena
text: Operational plan, not an architecture component.

speaker: Omar
text: I will check attestations Thursday. Priya, benchmark object fetch latency?

speaker: Priya
text: I can do it by next Monday.

speaker: Lena
text: Omar, write cache invalidation?

speaker: Omar
text: No, I cannot take another action this week. I am on incident rotation.

speaker: Lena
text: Fair. I will own invalidation note by Friday.

speaker: Priya
text: I can review; Lena owns write-up.

speaker: Omar
text: Kafka is supported by data platform, existing regional Kafka.

speaker: Lena
text: Retain Kafka, do not create a new cluster.

speaker: Priya
text: What if we switch to a CDN?

speaker: Omar
text: Private packages and per-build auth make that awkward. Not proposing a replacement.

speaker: Lena
text: Correct, no CDN in design.

speaker: Priya
text: I still have latency benchmark Monday.

speaker: Lena
text: I have invalidation Friday. Omar has attestation inventory Thursday.

speaker: Omar
text: Inventory only, not attestation design.

speaker: Lena
text: Got it.

speaker: Priya
text: macOS signing?

speaker: Lena
text: Existing signing unchanged; out of scope.

speaker: Omar
text: That is it.

speaker: Lena
text: One more storage choice: Postgres metadata is our baseline, but what if we move metadata to DynamoDB to avoid regional database scaling?

speaker: Omar
text: I can support DynamoDB for metadata; item access is by registry and digest, so the key fits.

speaker: Priya
text: Okay, let us accept DynamoDB metadata for the first region.

speaker: Lena
text: Actually, the retention queries need relational joins to build eviction batches. We should go back to Postgres metadata; the DynamoDB option is superseded.

speaker: Omar
text: Agreed, Postgres is still the right fit. Do not carry DynamoDB in the current design.

speaker: Lena
text: Closing after the build leads joined late; no design changes.
